 Order
The petition is listed for admission.
However, looking to the impugned order (Annexure P-1) which involves a purely legal issue, this petition is being heard and decided at the admission stage itself.

2. The brief facts of the matter are that the land of the petitioner was acquired for construction of a railway line and award dated 04.11.2019 was passed whereby certain compensation was ascertained to be paid to the petitioner.
Admittedly, compensation was paid to the petitioner in his bank account.

The petitioner, thereafter, moved an application in terms of Section 64 of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred as "Act of 2013") and requested to refer the matter to the Authority in the Bhagwat Prasad Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85300007/
1 matter of ascertainment of quantum of compensation.

sentences.text:
Application (Annexure P-2) was filed in this regard wherein it was clearly mentioned that the petitioner does not accept the quantum of compensation as mentioned in the award and therefore, the matter may be referred to the Authority in terms of Section 64 of the Act of 2013 for ascertainment of just compensation.
3.
The said application was filed on 02.12.2020 which was within the condonable time limit as per proviso to Section 64(2) of the Act of 2013.

The Collector has taken up the said application and rejected it by order (Annexure P-1) on the ground that since the petitioner has been paid the amount and he accepted the amount, hence, he cannot request reference of the matter for adjudication of adequacy of compensation.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the compensation was paid to the petitioner directly in his bank account and since compensation ascertained by the Collector was inadequate, he moved an application in terms of Section 64 to refer the matter to the Authority.

5. Per Contra, it is argued by learned counsel for the State that once a land loser gets an amount of compensation, he cannot move an application for referring the question of adequacy of compensation.

It is further argued by the State counsel that if the petitioner indeed wanted to get the matter referred to the Authority, then the petitioner was duty bound to first refund the compensation already received by him and only then he could have moved an application for referring the matter to the Authority to determine the quantum of compensation.
6.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, it is evident that the sole reason that weighed in the mind of Collector in refusing reference was that compensation amount has already been paid to the petitioner and as argued by learned State Counsel that amount is liable to be first refunded before making a request for enhancement.
7. The aforesaid logic adopted by the Collector and vehemently defended by the State counsel seems to be patently perverse to legal position.
The petitioner is not challenging the acquisition of his land but is seeking enhancement of compensation.
There is no provision of law as contained in the Act of 2013 that to seek enhancement of compensation, the land loser has to refuse even the compensation which is offered to him by the Collector.
There is no such mandate of law either in the Act of 2013 or in the earlier Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Section 64(1) of the Act of 2013 reads as under:-
"64. Reference to Authority-(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be,
whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:
Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority: Provided Bhagwat Prasad Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85300007/
2 further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be, requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days."
(Emphasis Supplied)
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The words 'who has not accepted award' have been misinterpreted by the Collector to mean that the person who has received the money offered by the Collector is deemed to have accepted the award.

When Section 64(1) of the Act of 2013 is read in its entirety, it is evident that the person who has not accepted the award has to file a written application to the Collector requesting to refer the matter.
The bare language of Section 64(1) itself means that a person who has not accepted the award is required to move an application for reference to the Collector.
This is the only mode of expressing his objection to the award.
There is no other mode laid down in the Act of 2013 to show objection of land loser to the compensation offered by the Collector, unless he has expressly given his acceptance to the award.

9. The aforesaid issue was considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the backdrop of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and it has been held that a person who has moved application for referring the application in terms of Section 18 of Act of 1894 is deemed to have expressed his objection to the award.

In Ajit Singh v. State of Punjab, (1994) 4 SCC 67 the Hon'ble Court held has under:-
"5. Having regard to the contiguity of these lands the High Court is correct in its valuation.

entities.text: Ajit Singh v. State of Punjab, (1994) 4 SCC 67
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Besides, the date of notification, issued under Section 4 of the Act, is October 4, 1978 while Exh. R-6 is nearer to it, namely, August 16, 1978, in comparison to Exh. A-6 dated January 14, 1977.
Inasmuch as the appellants have filed an application for reference under Section 18 of the Act that will manifest their intention.
Therefore, the protest against the award of the Collector is implied notwithstanding the acceptance of compensation.

The District Judge and the High Court, therefore, fell into patent error in denying the enhanced compensation to the appellants."
10.

In the case of SAIL v. Sutni Sangam, (2009) 16 SCC 1 the Hon'ble Apex Court has opined as under:
"69.
We may, however, hasten to add that we do not intend to lay down a law that the protest in regard to making of an award must be done in a manner specified expressly.

When an application for reference is filed, protest to the award is implicit as has been held by this Court in Ajit Singh v. State of Punjab [(1994) 4 SCC 67] :
(SCC p. 68, para 5) "5.

Besides, the date of notification, issued under Section 4 of the Act, is 4-10-1978 while Ext. R-6 is nearer to it, namely, 16-8-1978, in comparison to Ext. A-6 dated 14-1-1977.
Inasmuch as the appellants have filed an application for reference under Section 18 of the Act that will manifest their intention.

Therefore, the protest against the award of the Collector is implied notwithstanding the acceptance Bhagwat Prasad Tiwari vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85300007/
3 of compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The District Judge and the High Court, therefore, fell into patent error in denying the enhanced compensation to the appellants."
11. In view of the above, the impugned order (Annexure P-1) cannot be allowed to stand being patently perverse and contrary to legal position.
Consequently, the order (Annnexure P-1) is quashed.
The Collector, District Panna is directed to take up the application of the petitioner and refer the matter to the Authority in terms of Section 64 of the Act of 2013.
12. This court cannot lose sight of the fact that the land loser has been forced to approach this Court and involve in a litigation which was totally avoidable.
In view of this cost of Rs.5,000/- (Rs.Five Thousand only) is imposed on respondent No.1- Collector District Panna to be paid to the petitioner.
